v0.20.3 — a Bitcoin-style wallet RPC in the node, the Mesh Construction API, a container image

**Same chain, no coordinated update.** Replace the binary and restart; your data stays. Nothing in
this release changes consensus, the chain state or what nodes say to each other, so 0.20.x nodes
run side by side.

**One program.** The wallet RPC and the Mesh service are part of `helix` now. 0.20.2 shipped the
Mesh service as a separate `helix-mesh` binary; that binary is gone — run `helix mesh` instead,
with the same options.

**Bitcoin-style wallet RPC, served by the node**

- **A wallet that speaks Bitcoin Core's JSON-RPC** — method names, parameters, answers, error
  codes, HTTP Basic authentication, the `.cookie` file, batches — so an exchange connects Helix
  through the interface it already runs for Bitcoin and its descendants (#262, #263).
- **Configured like `bitcoin.conf`:** `helix.conf` in the wallet directory (`helix-wallet/` next to
  the node's database). `server=1` switches it on; `rpcbind`, `rpcport` (default
  `127.0.0.1:8547`), `rpcallowip`, `rpcuser`/`rpcpassword`, `rpcauth` (Bitcoin Core's salted hash),
  `rpccookiefile`, `walletnotify`, `blocknotify`, `paytxfee`, `maxtxfee`, `keypool`, sections
  `[main]`/`[test]`. Bitcoin options that mean nothing here (`txindex`, `dbcache`, …) are named in
  the log and passed over, so a copied `bitcoin.conf` works. **An unknown key stops the start**,
  and so does `zmqpub…` — Helix does not publish over ZMQ; use `walletnotify` and `blocknotify`.
- **Only this machine may connect unless `rpcallowip` says otherwise** (HTTP 403 for anyone else),
  and listening beyond this machine without `rpcallowip` stops the start, as in Bitcoin Core. In a
  container: `rpcallowip=172.16.0.0/12`.
- **`helix-cli`** is `bitcoin-cli` for it: the same binary under that name (a link to `helix`), or
  `helix rpc`. `-datadir`, `-conf`, `-rpcconnect`, `-rpcport`, `-rpcuser`, `-rpcpassword`,
  `-rpccookiefile`, `-named`, `-stdin`, `-stdinrpcpass`, `-rpcwait`, `-rpcclienttimeout`; an error
  exits with its code.
- **`walletnotify` / `blocknotify`** with `%s %b %h %w`, run for every change to a wallet
  transaction and once per round of new blocks.
- **Methods** besides the wallet's own: `getinfo`, `settxfee`, `getblock` (verbosity 1 and 2),
  `getrawtransaction` (verbose) — `vout` is whom the transaction's execution paid, read from the
  block's balance record, so **a failed transfer has no output** and a scanner never credits it.
- **`amountdecimals=8`** for an integration that stores eight decimals: amounts are shown with
  eight, rounded so a deposit is never shown larger and a send never smaller than it is; a ninth
  decimal sent in is refused.
- **An account per address, not coins:** each deposit is swept to the wallet's hot address once a
  block holds it, and listed as a `send` of 0 with its fee (`helix_sweep: true`). `sendmany` is
  refused — a Helix transaction pays one recipient.
- Every transaction the wallet signs is recorded before it is submitted and submitted again if it
  expires unincluded. On Linux and macOS the wallet directory is readable by its owner only.
- **Run it on an exchange's own node, not on a validator.** Against a node elsewhere:
  `helix wallet-rpc init` and `helix wallet-rpc serve`.

**Mesh (Rosetta) API**

- **The Construction API, for a transfer of HLX**: `derive`, `preprocess`, `metadata`, `payloads`,
  `combine`, `parse`, `hash`, `submit`. Curve and signature type `ml_dsa_65` (public key 1,952
  bytes, signature 3,309 bytes): sign the 32-byte payload with pure ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) and an
  empty context string. A memo goes through `preprocess`; the fee is the wallet's own rule, priced
  on the signed size, and a fee above 1 HLX is refused; `combine` verifies the signature (#264).
- **`helix mesh --offline`** serves only the steps around signing, for a machine that never talks
  to the network.
- Coinbase's Go SDK and `mesh-cli check:construction` do not sign ML-DSA yet; the flow is checked
  end to end against a real chain instead (both transfers of a fresh account, every balance exact).

**Listings and containers**

- **`GET /supply/circulating`, `/supply/total`, `/supply/max`** — a bare number in HLX, as listing
  sites expect (#262).
- **A container image: `ghcr.io/silvra-net/helix:0.20.3`** (and `:latest`), linux/amd64. It runs
  `helix start` in `/data` and carries `helix-cli`.

How an exchange or custodian puts this together: [Integrating
Helix](https://github.com/silvra-net/helix/blob/master/docs/exchange-integration.md).

**Helix is a testnet.** Its chain is reset when a release needs it, and HLX on it has no value.
